pageCache.pageTitle: CEO's Welcome - St Dunstan's Education Group
pageCache.text:
St Dunstan’s College is the beating heart of St Dunstan’s Education Group; a group of South London schools educating close to 2000 children across 6 sites and with a shared belief in educational excellence delivered differently.
It was on our Catford site, in 1888, that St Dunstan’s was founded as one of the world’s most pioneering schools for its time. A school that saw the value of placing science and technology into a curriculum when others would not. A school that believed children learned better by ‘finding out and doing’ when others preferred them to sit and listen. A school that settled on a humble blank shield as its metaphor for education – a blank canvas, upon which each child should carve their own journey and capture their unique individual identity.
Things have changed a great deal in the last 135 years. We are now in the heart of one of the most vibrant and diverse corners of the country. We are educating some 1250 boys and girls from ages 3–18.
We are one of the highest performing schools in the country, based on our academic, sporting and artistic outcomes. But some things never change.
We are once again recognised as being one of the most progressive schools in the UK, and at the forefront of educational thinking. From our pioneering Wellness Centre to our Forder Co-Curricular Programme, Sixth Form Diploma, St Dunstan’s Festival, and Let’s Talk About conference series, each initiative has been designed to play an integral part in the preparation of young people for success and happiness in its broadest sense.
Delivering excellence. differently is therefore baked into our thinking. It is a part of our organisational DNA. And whilst the array of awards, accolades and national recognition for our unique curriculum and culture are cherished, more important to us is what this means for the young people who are the privileged recipients of an education here.
Highly capable, ambitious young men and women who, as a consequence of an education that interweaves internationalism, platforms character development and equips young people with future-focused skill development, helps nurture and inspire tomorrow’s changemakers; changemakers with integrity, kindness and compassion at their core.
We believe that our approach to education speaks to tomorrow’s world. A world we can’t yet truly fathom but one that will need human values as much as it will intellectual agility. That will need courage and resilience. That will need creativity and deep thinking. This is what a St Dunstan’s education provides.
In recent years we have invested heavily in an estate that matches our approach to education and our ambitions for the future - a new Junior School, a STEM Centre for Excellence and Innovation, a dedicated Sixth Form Centre, and a state-of-the-art Performing Arts Theatre. Alongside this, our 21-acre Jubilee Grounds have been transformed into a hub for sport and community engagement, underpinning our groundbreaking gender-neutral sports programme, our unique partnership with Chelsea FC, and our extensive outreach across Lewisham.
Looking ahead, we are excited to have begun the redevelopment of the Plaza - creating a vibrant heart of the College campus - as well as unveiling our ambitious plans for a new Sport and Leisure Centre, which will further enhance opportunities for our community.
I hope this gives you a sense of the exciting, progressive environment that defines St Dunstan’s. I warmly invite you to visit us and to experience the energy of our community first-hand. During your time with us, I hope you will also enjoy learning more about our Junior and Senior Schools and meeting the Heads who lead them so ably. Both are exceptional leaders who embody the values of St Dunstan’s and are deeply committed to delivering an outstanding education for every child in their care as they bring excellence. differently. to life in their school communities.
Mr Nick Hewlett CEO, St Dunstan's Education Group

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from Head of St Dunstan's College
pageCache.text:
From the moment a pupil joins us, whether taking their first steps in Pre School, starting in Year 7, or entering the Sixth Form, a journey of discovery begins. We encourage every pupil to develop a deep understanding of who they are as an individual, while making the very most of the opportunities available to them at St Dunstan's College.
Proudly rooted in south-east London, St Dunstan's College is a highly successful co-educational independent school that challenges traditional perceptions of what an independent education can be. While our record-breaking GCSE and A Level results place us among the highest-performing schools in the country, St Dunstan's has always been about far more than academic outcomes. Successive pioneering Heads have shaped a progressive, research-informed education that challenges convention and delivers an experience that is broad, ambitious and future-focused.
That spirit has defined the College since its founding in 1888. Established with the bold vision of reimagining education, St Dunstan's was among the first schools in the world to introduce science and technology into the curriculum, thanks to a courageous group of governors determined to equip young people for the future.
Today, that same ambition continues to drive us. Alongside a remarkable academic transformation that has seen us ranked among the top independent schools in the UK, our students progress to an extraordinary range of destinations. From Oxford and Cambridge to art foundation courses, drama schools and conservatoires, they leave St Dunstan's prepared to pursue their individual passions and aspirations. In recent years, we have also been recognised with a number of prestigious awards, including Co-educational School of the Year, Independent School of the Year, Most Progressive Independent School in London, Most Progressive Independent School in South-East England, and Best Diversity and Inclusion in Sport.
At the heart of a St Dunstan's education is a commitment to developing thoughtful, reflective and principled young people. We encourage our students to consider not only what they want to achieve, but also the kind of people they wish to become.
By exploring the values that shape their decisions and actions, they develop the confidence, character and sense of purpose needed to thrive as global citizens in a rapidly changing world.
Across our Junior School, Senior School and Sixth Form, every stage of the St Dunstan's journey offers something distinctive. I look forward to welcoming you to one of our Open Days or Discovery Tours, where you can experience the warmth, energy and ambition of our community for yourself.
Ms Jade McLellan Head of St Dunstan's College

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from Head of Junior School at St Dunstan's College
pageCache.text:
Welcome to the Junior School, where pupils make their first marks on the blank canvas of their St Dunstan’s shield as they begin their College adventure.
It is here that children learn who they are and discover a true love of lifelong learning from the very earliest stages of their education.
Our academic ambition is cultivated through a balance of challenge, rigour, immersive learning experiences and independent exploration. Our broad and engaging curriculum is unapologetically aspirational for every pupil, regardless of their starting point, and equips them with the skills needed to thrive as proactive global citizens in a rapidly changing world.
Pupils quickly see that through learning, they gain a deeper understanding of who they are, what they can achieve, and what they may accomplish in the future.
At St Dunstan’s, we are brave in the choices we make for our pupils. We can do this because of the strong, trusting relationships we hold with parents and carers, who choose our school because of the way we nurture natural curiosity and support children in discovering where and how they fit into the world. Learning here is never restricted to the classroom. It takes place everywhere: through our co-curricular Forder Programme (with over 90 activities each week), performing on professional stages, overcoming fears on residential trips, developing teamwork on the sports field, or deepening an understanding of the natural world in our Woodland Classroom.
We are a co-educational Junior School for children from Pre-School to Year 6, and we take pride in a modern, forward-thinking curriculum taught by our highly skilled teachers. Every day is different, and every experience is designed to encourage children to be creative, curious and courageous. This holistic approach ensures pupils feel safe, happy and fulfilled, while growing into well-rounded individuals who are prepared to succeed.
As part of the wider College, our pupils benefit from the consistency of a Form Teacher and the specialist expertise and facilities of the Senior School. From art, drama and music, to swimming, sport, design technology, computing, languages and the Stuart Curriculum (PSHEE), children make rapid progress across all areas. We are particularly proud of our bespoke 'Albam Exorna' Curriculum - based around six key strands (Healthy Lifestyle and Living, Finance and Enterprise, Sustainability, Technology and Innovation, Community and Character and Personal Development). It has been designed thoughtfully to prepare children with the life skills they need to thrive in tomorrow's world. Through this exposure, they not only achieve academically but also discover new passions, develop confidence in their skills, and thrive within strong teacher-pupil relationships.
Above all, our Junior School is a community full of energy and joy. Stories are shared, friendships are made, and children are given the freedom to grow as individuals whilst being part of something bigger.
The best way to experience the spirit of St Dunstan’s is to visit us in person. I warmly invite you to join us for one of our discovery mornings or our College Open Day, where you will see first-hand how unique and exciting education is here at St Dunstan’s Junior School. I look forward to welcoming you soon.
Miss Laura Whitwood Head of Junior School

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from Head of Senior School at St Dunstan's College
pageCache.text:
Welcome to the Senior School, a progressive and ambitious community where young people are encouraged to think deeply, act with integrity, and embrace the opportunities that lie ahead. These are some of the most important years in a child's development, and our aim is to ensure that every student leaves with not only outstanding academic outcomes, but also the confidence, character and curiosity to thrive in an ever-changing world.
At St Dunstan's, we believe that a great education extends far beyond the classroom. While academic achievement is a hallmark of our success, we are equally committed to nurturing individuality, fostering meaningful relationships, and helping every student discover their passions and potential. Guided by four core principles, our Senior School experience is designed to challenge, inspire and empower.
Academic Excellence
Academic excellence at St Dunstan's is about far more than securing excellent examination results. It is about cultivating intellectual curiosity, developing depth of understanding, and helping students become confident, independent learners.
Our evidence-informed approach to teaching draws on the latest pedagogical research and cognitive science, equipping students with the knowledge, skills and habits that enable them to flourish academically. We encourage them to ask questions, embrace challenge, think critically and develop the intellectual resilience needed for lifelong learning.
Innovation
Innovation has been part of the St Dunstan's story since our founding, and it continues to shape how we prepare young people for the future.
From our pioneering AI Education and Ethics programme to our distinctive Stuart and Usherwood curricula, we are committed to ensuring education remains relevant to the world our students are growing up in. Innovation extends beyond technology; it influences how we approach wellbeing, resilience, personal development and the wider question of what it means to live a fulfilled and purposeful life.
We are unafraid to explore the issues that matter, because we believe the best education is both forward-thinking and deeply human.
Integrity
Alongside academic success, we place great importance on developing young people who are thoughtful, principled and socially aware. Through leadership opportunities, volunteering programmes and collaborative projects, students learn the value of listening, understanding different perspectives and working together to create positive change. We want our students to leave St Dunstan's with a strong sense of responsibility, empathy and purpose, having benefited from our distinctive South London identity.
Individuality
We are proud to nurture every child and to support them to find their own diverse passions and interests, rather than expecting to all fit the same mould.
Our extensive Forder co-curricular programme encourages every student to explore their interests, discover new talents and challenge themselves beyond the classroom. Whether through sport, music, drama, debating, community action or countless other opportunities, students are supported to shape an educational journey that reflects their own ambitions, talents and aspirations.
By nurturing individuality, we help young people grow into confident and authentic versions of themselves.
These four principles are only part of what makes the St Dunstan's Senior School experience distinctive. As you explore our website, you'll discover more about our innovative curriculum, exceptional pastoral care, rich co-curricular opportunities and the vibrant community that underpins everything we do.
We warmly invite you to visit us at an Open Event or Discovery Tour and experience first-hand the energy, ambition and sense of belonging that define life at St Dunstan's. Click here to see upcoming dates.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to the Sixth Form - St Dunstan's College
pageCache.text:
At St Dunstan’s Sixth Form, excellence is more than exam results: it is a way of thinking and living.
We believe that true success combines intellectual rigour with moral integrity and the courage to do things differently. Here, education is not just about what you achieve, but about the kind of person you become.
These are transformative years. Our students grow in independence, ambition, and character as they prepare to take their place in the world. They are encouraged to think boldly, act responsibly, and lead with vision, qualities that define our Sixth Form community. Friendships are forged through challenge and opportunity, whether competing in national design competitions, volunteering locally, curating our own summer festival, or learning from alumni who are leaders in their fields.
The results speak for themselves. Our outstanding A Level outcomes place St Dunstan’s among the top 25 schools in the UK. National recognition, including success at the TES Schools Awards, celebrates the creativity, innovation, and integrity that set our students apart.
To join St Dunstan’s is to embark on a collaborative journey of discovery, challenge, and growth—stepping with confidence into your own future.
Ms Jade McLellan Head of Senior School
Mr Alex Brewer Head of Sixth Form

pageCache.pageTitle: Sciences and the Arts both hit record highs for Year 11 2026 | Default Post Page
pageCache.text:
Sciences and the Arts both hit record highs as St Dunstan's College celebrates outstanding GCSE Results
From Art & Design Engineering to the Sciences, Year 11 results show a school where intellectual rigour and creative achievement go hand in hand — a week after the College's record-breaking A Level results.
St Dunstan's College is celebrating an outstanding set of GCSE results this year, with 59% of all grades awarded at the top 9/8 (A**/A*), 95% at grade 9–6 (A*–B), and an average grade of 7.6 across the cohort. The results follow the College's record-breaking A Level outcomes announced last week, continuing an upward trajectory across both key stages.
What stands out this year is the breadth of that success. Alongside the College's impressive Science results including Biology students achieving 92% at grade 9–7 (A*–A), Art and Design Engineering achieved a perfect 100% at 9–7, with Geography (98%), Music (95%) and French (94%) close behind. Across all subjects, 82% of grades were awarded at 9–7 (A*–A), and 36% of students achieved grade 7 or above in every GCSE they sat.
For a school that places equal weight on core subjects and the creative and modern languages curriculum, the results are a marker of a genuinely rounded, progressive education, where pupils are encouraged to pursue rigorous science and design alongside music, art and language, rather than being asked to choose between them.
Jade McLellan, Head of Senior School, commented:
It has been a wonderful morning celebrating exceptional GCSE results across the board, with so much excitement from our students, seeing what the last five years of hard work has delivered. We are particularly proud that this success happens across such a range of subjects, from core subjects to the creatives. We look forward to supporting them with next stage of their academic journey in the Sixth Form to prepare for university and the challenges of the world of work!
The breadth of achievement is reflected in the students themselves. Imani, who achieved all 9s and two 8s, is staying on to study Physics, Chemistry, Further Maths and Maths at A Level:
I've really been part of St Dunstan's for a long time now and it's been fantastic. I think what makes it special is the support you're given and the amount of different opportunities outside of academic life as well.
Cillian, who achieved all 8s and 9s, is moving into the Sixth Form to study Politics, Religion, Philosophy & Ethics, Classics and English:
It's a really good atmosphere for learning and everyone's really friendly, and all of the teachers are really supportive and helpful.
Parents are seeing the same balance play out at home.
Ivy, who achieved eight 9s and one 8 and is staying on to study Maths, English, Psychology and Economics, is one of several Year 11 students whose time at the College so far has spanned sport, the arts and academics alike. Her father said:
We chose St Dunstan's because we heard great things about how holistic it was — from the sports to the acting to the music and then the level of the education. Each teacher, each department has really taken her as an individual and helped nurture her through to these exams.
Charlie's father, whose son achieved mostly grade 8s and is moving up to study History at A Level, furthered the point:
When we came and looked at St Dunstan's it was immediately apparent that the quality of teaching was absolutely superb. Quite often schools have a marketing approach and then when you're in the school, the real approach can sometimes be quite different. But in this case it hasn't at all. It’s gone above and beyond. The school's very strong in its arts, in its music and drama, and so he's been able to do lots of things from sports to academic to arts, and every year it's got better and better for him.
Noah’s mother reflected on the level of support and inclusivity of the school:
We love the inclusivity, the pastoral care. St Dunstan's is a school that is multifaceted, and the breadth of children that are here is a huge strength. You can come here and you can find whatever it is that you love and do well. It is a school that encourages everyone to follow what they want to do and whatever that path is, is accommodated.
Year 11 students now progress into St Dunstan's Sixth Form alongside new joiners from local state schools across south-east London; rooted in the same community that shaped their GCSE years, and ready for whatever comes next.
The College is continuing to develop its Sixth Form offer to reflect the world beyond education. This September sees the launch of the Nexus Series, an employability and leadership masterclass programme designed to build the commercial awareness and professional skills students need for a graduate market increasingly shaped by AI-enabled recruitment. The programme sits alongside plans for a new Sixth Form Centre, part of a wider Sports & Leisure complex renovation due to open in 2028.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Dunstan's College, leading the way in MFL provision | Default Post Page
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages teacher Kate Melhorn was recently invited to speak at the Association for Language Learning, advising fellow senior educators and other top schools from around the country in developing career skills and pathways within MFL.
This followed the remarkable success of the ‘Careers in Languages’ evening at St Dunstan’s College, which was attended by hundreds of students not only from St Dunstan’s but also other local secondary schools.
Presenting to Heads of Department and curriculum leaders for languages from around the UK, Kate’s talk at the Association for Language Learning was entitled “Boosting A-Level languages: Practical strategies that work”, sharing how other schools could replicate elements of the careers event in their own school or region, helping to boost take-up of languages at A-Level.
Speaking about the importance of studying languages at A-Level, particularly in our ever-changing digital world, Kate said: “The number of students studying languages in the UK to A level and beyond is generally in decline across both the independent and state sectors.”
“Studying a language to a high-level fosters empathy as well as improving critical thinking and problem-solving abilities."
"If we look at AI in 2026 it is apparent that we desperately need more professionals with expertise in STEM that also possess high levels of empathy and the ability to view the world from multiple perspectives.”
Regarding the next Careers in Languages event, which will take place at St Dunstan’s College on the evening of Thursday 8 October 2026, Kate said: “It will be even bigger and better than last time, and we will have a theatrical element in addition to our exciting language taster sessions and inspiring speakers.”
Head of Futures, Rebecca Redding, said: “We are delighted that our Careers in Languages event has found so much success, and has been able to inspire other schools.”
“It is a reflection of the deep importance we place on readying students for the job market, introducing students on the wide range of opportunities that are available to them, and giving them the tools and skills to thrive in the rapidly changing world of work.”
If you would be interested in talking at the next Careers in Languages evening on Thursday 8 October 2026 and helping to inspire the next generation of polyglots, please get in touch with Kate Melhorn at kmelhorn@stdunstans.org.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Stellar A Level results for impressive 2026 Year 13 cohort | Default Post Page
pageCache.text:
On our crest, three quarters of the shield are left deliberately blank as a physical expression of the College’s 138-year-old motto, Albam Exorna (‘adorn the white’), an instruction to every pupil to make their own mark, in their own way. This year’s leavers appear to have taken it literally: as we celebrate the best A Level results in our history, with 28% of grades awarded the top A* grade, our students are heading everywhere from Oxbridge and Medical School to the Army, a City degree apprenticeship and a conservatoire.
This year, 92% of all grades achieved were A*–B, while an outstanding 29% were graded A* and 70% of grades were A*–A, maintaining the College's exceptional academic performance and reinforcing its reputation for educational excellence.
While the grades are exceptional, they are only part of our story at St Dunstan’s. The College’s approach is built around developing the individual as much as the academic; young people who leave not only with exceptional qualifications, but with the confidence, character and curiosity to chart a path that is genuinely their own. The result is a school rooted in its South London community but preparing its students for a world well beyond Catford.
Speaking about the record-breaking results, Jade McLellan, Head of Senior School, said:
These results are a tremendous achievement for our students and staff, and one which reflects the ambition, curiosity and resilience that defines our school community. We are incredibly proud that our young people have secured such outstanding outcomes whilst embracing everything that makes a St Dunstan's education distinctive. We are committed to developing confident, compassionate and capable young people who are prepared not only for university, but for meaningful lives and careers beyond it. Seeing our students progress to such an exciting range of destinations is a great measure of that success."
Six pupils achieved at least three straight A*s. But it is the breadth of what happens next that tells the fuller story, each leaver forging their own path:
T’iama achieved 4A*s and is heading to LSE to study Data Science “I feel lost for words. I joined St Dunstan’s in Year 12 and since then they have helped nurture my passions. The school environment is very caring and welcoming and there’s a wide variety of subjects. Teachers always made time for me if I needed help. They also really helped me with supra curriculars and encouraged us to focus on ourselves as individuals not just academically.”
Julia (left) achieved 3A*s and goes on to study English Literature at Durham University “I’m feeling really overwhelmed with joy and I’m really grateful and happy that all the hard work paid off. The community here is so lovely. I joined here in Year 7 as a Drama Scholar, and I had no idea that in seven years I’d be leaving with an A* in Drama. St Dunstan’s has prepared me in every way possible for the next step in my journey, so I don’t feel scared at all!”
Patrick (left) achieved A*A*A and is embarking on a gap year before Medical School “I joined St Dunstan’s in Year 12. It’s been a whole mass of opportunities since. The teachers were completely supportive of what I chose. Everything I needed to function and thrive is here. This school has given me the opportunity to go places.”
Matilda achieved A*AA “I got into Loughborough, my first choice, to study Natural Sciences, but I will be taking a year out to join the Army as an Officer and I’m so excited about all of it. I joined St Dunstan’s in Year 7 and it’s been an amazing journey – I’ve done so much. The school has so much to offer. It’s not just about the academics, it’s about the whole person and who you can become.”
Rafferty (left, with Mr Brewer, Head of Sixth Form) achieved 3A*s in Maths, Physics & DT and is heading to the University of Manchester to study Electrical Engineering. “I’m really pleased with myself. I didn’t expect it. I’ve had a great time at St Dunstan’s. It’s a very welcoming place to be and I enjoyed A Levels, studying the subjects I love. I feel I’ve grown a lot as a person as well as learning a lot.”
Matthew achieved 3A*s and is going to study Economics at the University of Warwick “I’m over the moon to be honest. The teachers here are so caring – they want you to do well and they believe in you, which means you can believe in yourself. The community here is immense. I couldn’t see myself being anywhere else – it’s such a big part of my life now. There’s so much joy and happiness, which is encapsulated today - all the smiles on everyone’s faces and all the joy is just amazing to see.”
Alex Brewer, Head of Sixth Form, added:
Today's results tell only part of the story. What makes me most proud is seeing each student leave with a destination that genuinely reflects their ambitions, whether that's Oxbridge, Medical School, a conservatoire, Art Foundation or a highly competitive degree apprenticeship. The world our students are entering is changing rapidly, and it is our responsibility to ensure they are equipped for it. Alongside academic excellence, we place real emphasis on developing the skills, adaptability and confidence that will enable our students to flourish throughout their careers."
Opportunity remains central to the College's ethos. Around one in twelve St Dunstan's students currently benefit from means-tested bursary support, enabling talented young people from a wide range of backgrounds to access an independent education.
Outgoing Head of School, Emmanuel, who joined St Dunstan's Sixth Form from a local comprehensive school through the College's bursary programme, will now embark on a degree apprenticeship with leading private bank, UBS. He said:
"St Dunstan’s really opened my eyes and exposed me to different things. Leaving now as outgoing Head of School is honestly a bittersweet moment because I’ll miss everyone here, but it’s also exciting to go onto a new chapter and see what the future holds."
This year has also seen the College receive a string of external accolades, the most recent being from The Telegraph who awarded St Dunstan's its highest 'Very Good' rating for value among independent schools, placing the College amongst the leading schools in London for the quality of education delivered relative to its fees. Awards received earlier this year include Top 100 in The Times Parent Power league table, a commendation for London School of the Year (Independent Schools of the Year) and wins for both Academic Excellence and Sporting Development (Private Education Awards), recognising the breadth of its provision beyond examination results alone.

The wraparound care at St Dunstan's Junior School is designed to offer families flexibility, peace of mind, and truly outstanding provision.
Before-school care begins at 0745 and is run by our own trusted Junior School support staff - familiar faces who know the children well and create a calm, welcoming start to the day. After School Care is delivered by the brilliant team at Munchkins Sports, who bring energy, creativity, and a wide range of fun activities to keep children engaged from the end of the school day until 1800.
What sets our wraparound care apart is its flexibility. We make it a priority to never cap numbers, so every child from Pre-School to Year 6 is welcome whenever the need arises, and we can staff these numbers accordingly.
The team is highly trained, enthusiastic, and passionate about creating a safe, enjoyable environment where children genuinely want to be. In fact, many families choose to sign up even when they do not need it, simply because their children love it so much.
We also work hard to ensure our pricing remains competitive and fair, recognising the demands of busy family life. At St Dunstan’s, wraparound care is not just an ‘add-on;’ it is an essential part of our offering.

Connections Beyond the Classroom
Our outreach activities and local partnerships play a vital role in enriching student learning, widening opportunities, and strengthening the communities we serve.
By working collaboratively with local organisations, charities, businesses, and educational institutions, we foster shared knowledge, mutual support, and real-world experiences that help our students grow into confident, compassionate, and socially responsible individuals.
Please read our latest Outreach impact reports below:
Spotlight on Lewisham Young Leaders Academy (LYLA)
St Dunstan's College has been supporting the Lewisham Young Leaders Academy for disadvantaged Black African, Black Caribbean and dual heritage children aged 8-18 since its inception in 2019. LYLA provides leadership skills through positive role modelling, exploration of history and provision of informal academic support .
LYLA is an extraordinary and enriching environment where learning extends beyond the conventional boundaries. It offers a platform to forge friendships, embark on exciting trips, and engage in captivating workshops. Here, your mind is nurtured to think beyond limitations, encouraging constant exploration. Your unique talents are celebrated, fostering a sense of belonging akin to a close-knit family. Anticipating each weekly visit fills me with excitement, as it equips me with invaluable tools for navigating daily life. Every session brings forth fresh opportunities for growth, which I deeply appreciate.
LYLA serves as a powerful motivator for black youth, empowering them to overcome obstacles and strive for the most promising prospects. Being part of this remarkable community is a true blessing, one that should be cherished with gratitude.'
Rachel "Hope" Limba, LYLA volunteer and St Dustan's student
Spotlight on Chelsea FC Foundation partnership
This exciting collaboration between St Dunstan's College and one of the world's leading football and community development organisations gives pupils access to exceptional coaching, training programmes and unique opportunities to develop both on and off the pitch.
Through the partnership, pupils of all ages benefit from expert coaching delivered by Chelsea FC Foundation staff, who work closely with the College’s sports department to nurture talent, build skills and inspire a lifelong enjoyment of sport. Sessions are designed to promote teamwork, resilience and confidence, ensuring that pupils develop as well-rounded individuals as well as athletes.
In addition to football training, the partnership extends to a range of educational and enrichment opportunities. Workshops, leadership sessions and community initiatives allow pupils to explore broader aspects of sport, health and wellbeing, linking closely with the College’s values of courage, creativity, confidence, compassion and curiosity.
The collaboration with Chelsea FC Foundation strengthens the College’s commitment to offering an innovative and diverse co-curricular programme. Whether pupils are pursuing football at an elite level or simply enjoy participating for fitness and fun, this partnership ensures that every child can experience the very best in sporting provision.
Spotlight on the Catford Weekender
The Catford Weekender is a community festival in Lewisham which was launched for the first time in June 2024 by St Dunstan’s College.
It has since been supported by many local sponsors including 4TY Planning Ltd, Barton Knight, Munchkins and Barton Knight.
This year we are thrilled that our Headline Sponsors are Judge & Priestly, a firm of solicitors acting for individuals, businesses and local authorities in Bromley, Beckenham, Blackheath, Sidcup and central London.
If you would like to get involved or donate to any of our outreach projects, please contact Isabelle Blake-James, Director of Philanthropy, at philanthropy@stdunstans.org.uk.
How to donate
There are a number of ways you can support St Dunstan’s College. All donations, large or small, are precious and meaningful regardless of the amount. You can give in a number of ways.

The beginnings
A school has been associated with the parish of St Dunstan’s in the East as far back as 1446. As far as we can tell, this school ran, intermittingly, until the early 16th century, and provided an education for girls and boys aged 7-11, in heart of the City of London.
In the Victorian period, and amidst the opportunities of the Industrial Revolution, the church parishioners of St Dunstan’s in the East were confident that they could re-establish a school that would meet the highest educational standards of the day. It would be both a boarding and day school and would be located outside the City, whilst still accessible by the new and growing railway network. By 1854, the current Catford site was decided upon as the ideal location.
At the end of the 19th century there was an increasing emphasis on the importance of science and technology. As such, the first Governing Body of St Dunstan’s made the progressive decision that their new school should emphasise this. They chose as their first Headmaster, a chemist named Charles Maddock Stuart. Mr Stuart was a proponent of heuristic (hands on) education. St Dunstan’s College was the first school in the country to be designed with laboratories in it and the curriculum featured more than three times that normally allotted to the sciences and experimentation in order that pupils could ‘find out’ and ‘do’. Mr Stuart once said ‘it is not so much what a boy learns that is important, but how he learns it’.
From its opening in 1888, St Dunstan’s set itself apart from other independent schools, both by its innovative technical curriculum and by the determination to be an accessible school, supporting families from a range of different backgrounds and incomes.
The War Years
It was in 1898 that St Dunstan’s established its first military drill programme, in response to the Boer War. By 1910, more than half of all pupils participated in the Officer Training Corps, opening many opportunities to become an officer after their examinations.
When the call to arms came in 1914, 977 former and current St Dunstan’s pupils and staff signed up to join. By the end of the war, 237 would never return home, amongst the highest percentage of casualties of any independent school in the United Kingdom. Shortly thereafter, war memorials were established at St. George’s Church in Ypres, the battlefield at Loos, and in the Great Hall at St Dunstan’s. The College’s memorial reads ‘Albam Exornurant’ a modification of the slogan ‘Albam Exorna’, and reminding us that ‘They Adorned the White’ through their extraordinary service and commitment to school and country.
The inter-war years were filled with great challenges, as well as opportunities. Frank Forder, the second Headmaster of St Dunstan’s, introduced the importance of the outdoors and sport to the curriculum, believing that mind and body were both in need of education. Revd Forder’s impact on the College continues today, as we dedicate our co-curricular programme to his name. Following Revd Forder was John Usherwood, who took great efforts to update the College’s facilities and prepare pupils for whatever great challenges lay ahead.
During the Second World War, life was particularly hard for the pupils of St Dunstan’s. In September of 1939 they were evacuated to Reigate, where they would spend most of the war, except for a second evacuation in 1944 to Wales. The laboratory facilities that pupils were used to at St Dunstan’s gave way to makeshift chemistry sets in a converted bathroom; playing fields had to be shared with bomb shelters.
Growth and Change
The end of the Wars ushered in a time of relative prosperity. This new era of hope and forward momentum was overseen by William Hecker, who wanted to ensure a better future for pupils after such a traumatic period. 1953 - 1972 saw the most rapid growth and development at the College since its foundation.
The new Swimming Pool, constructed in 1955, gave pupils access to both the new challenge of swimming, as a sport, and also the luxury of cooling off during warmer months.
The Pavilion was constructed in 1958 and came about as a consequence of the increased requirement for physical education and sport in the National Curriculum. The new dining facilities demonstrated the ambition for innovation.
The current Refectory, constructed in 1961, is one of only four hyperbolic paraboloid structures built in the world. New was the order of the day.
The trend for enhancement continued under Richard Pedley and Brian Dance, who between them brought about new facilities for Music and Physics in 1971 and expanded the facilities for young pupils, with the completion of the Prep Block in 1973. The rapid pace of growth saw the College roll peak in 1974, with 939 pupils. In 1981, Mr Dance chose to expand the diversity of the pupil population by accommodating families who were traditionally unable to afford private education. It was in this period that the College became increasingly anchored to its rich history with the City of London. The ceremony of the Beating of the Bounds was re-introduced in 1978, incorporating the ruins of St Dunstan’s in the East and celebrating the medieval roots of the College.
New Beginnings
All of the expansion and development of the second half of the 20thCentury created a strong platform from which St Dunstan’s could innovate. In 1994, the College expanded its roll to include a Pre-Prep school for ages 4 and above. In an even bolder leap forward, that same year, St Dunstan’s became a co-educational school, with the gradual integration of girls at all ages. The new St Dunstan’s could now take a holistic approach to the education of all pupils, of whatever age, background or gender, and prepare individuals for the challenges and opportunities of a rapidly changing world.
Under David Moore, there was an understanding that these changes necessarily called for an expansion of activities. This began in 1996 with the completion of a new Sports Hall designed to service not just rugby and cricket, but the variety of physical education required to meet the interests of a diverse and coeducational pupil body. The College took an increasingly modern and global approach to education, with an increased emphasis on trips abroad and new modern languages and computing being introduced to the curriculum. The College’s arts programme expanded, with a new performance space created above the Great Hall, and the very first Arts Festival held in 1994.
Ian Davies was deeply committed to internationalism and the importance of a rounded education, despite the national drive for increased emphasis on public examination. The International Baccalaureate was introduced in 2004.
Nearly ten years after girls were first accepted to the school, the first Headmistress was appointed. Jane Davies forged strong links across the breadth of the St Dunstan’s community, working closely with Old Dunstonian Association and the Family Society (as the Friends of St Dunstan’s was formerly known).
St Dunstan’s was able to celebrate its 125thAnniversary in particular style, and the addition of the Jubilee Ground, on Catford Green, in 2012, signalled a new era for St Dunstan’s position within the local community. A College, built on its relationship with the City of London, could continue its traditions of collaboration, innovation and service.
New developments and navigating a global pandemic
In 2020, St Dunstan’s faced its greatest disruption since the war years, as the world faced the global pandemic, Coronavirus. For the first time since the war, the College gates were closed and in late March, the entire St Dunstan’s experience went virtual.
Always wanting to lead the way, St Dunstan’s was one of the first schools in the area to move its entire academic and co-curricular programme online.
All lessons were delivered via remote platforms, and an ongoing commitment to virtual pastoral and cocurricular provision during the two lockdowns ensured pupils and staff felt connected and supported despite all the various challenges brought to bear through such isolating times.
Despite the challenges of a global pandemic, the same year marked the start of the most significant developments of the school site since 1888.
A new Junior School, STEM Centre for Excellence and Innovation and Sixth Form Centre was built, and the school welcomed back Dunstonian and Nobel Prize winner, Martin Evans, for the grand opening.
Alongside the new spaces, other areas of the College were redeveloped which opened the doors to a Performing Arts Centre with a theatre space and two outside pond areas.
National Awards
In recent years, the College's forward-thinking education has also won the endorsement of many prestigious awards. St Dunstan's was named Co-educational School of the Year at the Independent Schools of the Year Awards 2020, Most Nurturing Independent School at the Private Education Awards 2022, and Independent Senior School of the Year at the Tes Schools Awards 2022. The College was also recognised as Most Progressive School in London at the Private Education Awards 2023, followed by Most Progressive School in South-East England in 2024. In addition, St Dunstan’s won Outstanding Fundraising Achievement at the Independent Schools of the Year Awards 2023 and received the Diversity and Inclusion in Sport Award from Education Choices Magazine in both 2024 and 2025.
Most recently, the College was nominated once again for Senior School of the Year at the Tes Schools Awards 2025.
Celebrating 30 years of Coeducation
In 2024, St Dunstan’s College proudly celebrated 30 years of co-education. Since welcoming the first cohort of girls in 1994, the College has flourished as a truly inclusive and progressive community, where young people of all backgrounds learn, grow and thrive together. To mark the anniversary, the Dunstonian Association welcomed back the families of the original first girls’ cohort for a special family day, which included recreating the iconic first photograph on the College’s front steps. The occasion offered an opportunity to reflect on three decades of achievement, innovation, and change, while reaffirming the College’s commitment to providing an education that prepares all pupils to excel in the modern world.
Heads of St Dunstan's College
Rev Frank G. Forder, 1922-1930
